visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a static, extreme close-up of a brownish, translucent mineral specimen mounted on a small mound of white adhesive putty. The lighting is bright and directional, revealing the internal grain and rough, waxy surface of the stone, which bears a striking resemblance to a piece of cooked fat. Subtitles appear at the bottom over a dark blue background. (2) The lighting suddenly shifts to ultraviolet (UV), causing the mineral to emit an intense, multi-colored glow. Layers of neon green, vivid yellow, and deep purple appear within the stone's structure. The camera remains focused on the specimen, which is slowly rotated to show its fluorescent properties from different angles against a black background. (3) A sequence of shots displays multiple smaller specimens of the same mineral, all showing similar layered fluorescence under UV light. The camera alternates between medium close-ups of the group and extreme macro shots of individual glowing layers, highlighting the intricate geological patterns. The setting remains a controlled, dark studio environment. (4) The video concludes with a final montage of various Hokkaidoite specimens. The camera zooms in and out on the vibrant green and yellow glowing bands. The background features consistent technical overlays and social media handles, while the lighting remains in the UV spectrum to emphasize the mineral's rare optical characteristics.
